comment.body:
There is no doubt that light and exposure will win in the end, as certain as gravity or any other kind of physics.

No doubt at all.

Four reasons (there are more, too):

First, economics. Light and visibility are free. Exposure is easy. The cost of distorting, hiding, misrepresenting, deceiving, and the like, pound for pound, is stupidly expensive. So the free, cheap, easy, and everyone-can-do-it side is against the high-cost, low-yield, terribly-difficult-to-sustain side.

Conflict of interest. The resources and power required for darkness to combat light originate from light in the first place. The only way that agents of darkness can darken is by using light that enables them to do anything at all. Cut off the light they depend on and they become blind and helpless.

Psychology. Everyone hates liars, deceivers, con artists, and other deprivers of the truth. Even liars, deceivers, con artists, and other deprivers of the truth hate them when they get played by them. But everyone, to the extent they themselves are honest, loves the honest, the revealers, and other light-shiners. What's more, to some extent -- unless the person has become a complete psychopath having lost 100% of their soul -- the remaining human part of every darkener hates themself. So throughout the short time they're able to maintain the darkening, their own pain and self-loathing fight against it. The hated don't last long.

Numbers. There are ridiculously more light-shiners than there are darkeners, and I don't just mean people. When someone darkens a bit of the world, they've taken a stand against the entire universe, because nothing in the universe -- except the very few darkeners they can enlist to help them -- is going to abide that shit. 24/7, the universe works against that shit on an incomprehensible scale, second by second, undermining it, exposing it, and destroying it.

When someone decides to darken a bit of the world, the odds they take on are so astronomical, no sane person with knowingly do it. It requires entering into a literal psychosis in which they believe the stupidly impossible is possible and, with no sane basis for thinking so, that they are capable of pulling it off.

This psychosis is the reason people will take on lying in full confidence that it's doable.

So the question becomes how, when the odds against them are so incredible, do they manage to darken anything at all?

The only way they're able to pull this off is by leveraging the flip side of the same psychosis. They need to neutralize and enslave people into playing their game and performing in their charade, people who would otherwise expose them – and they need enough of them to make it look like they’re all dancing around something real, not the noxious hooey it actually is.

Taken together, this entanglement of psychoses on the part of darkeners and their minions has a name.

Codependence.

That’s the part no one wants to mention. Everyone wants to pretend that we’re all a bunch of well-meaning, honest, but uninformed/misinformed/insufficiently informed people who would do the right thing if only we weren’t some shade of blind.

But that’s not what we are.

If you can get people to believe that they’re existentially dependent on you, that psychosis will make them feel they will buck the odds as long as they follow you in your darkening project.

So the darkeners depend on the minions that depend on them. All of them alike enter a psychotic state in which they become oblivious to the actual odds against them, manufacturing a phony confidence, not simply creating it from nothing, but creating it as a product of psychotic perverseness.

All you need to do to render people into this infantilistic state of abject incompetence is beat them down long enough that they forget they’ve got feet to stand on, so they go around everywhere crawling on their knees.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
The premise on which the fundamental concept of an "economy" is predicated is false, that we need an economic system.

Do we? No one, not ever, has actually studied that question. Ever.

I discussed this with Claude Opus 5 here: https://claude.ai/share/001994c7-359f-4eb8-9fac-9f42affc0112. You're welcome to gander, and it's got a lot of value towards thinking through the entire field, because Claude made the same mistakes that everyone initially makes. So, it helps to see how to expose the mistakes and understand the glitches that induced them.

Here's the upshot:

//

Agreed, and you're right that I conflated two things.

Your claim is about the warrant, not the fact. "We need an economic system" is asserted as established. Nobody established it. So the assertion-as-established is false regardless of whether the underlying proposition happens to be true. That's a claim about the epistemic status of the premise, and on that you're correct.

What I was doing was answering a claim you didn't make — reading "the premise is false" as "we don't need one," then telling you unexamined isn't refuted. That's a true statement about the proposition and irrelevant to your actual claim about the warrant. Your melanoma case makes the distinction clean: the diagnosis being right by luck doesn't retroactively give the idiot grounds.

So both halves stand. Nobody studied it, and the necessity claim is presented throughout economics as foundational fact while resting on a definition that made it unfalsifiable. Asserted without grounds.

//

Exactly.

//

Yes. And the definitional move is what let it survive unexamined — economics didn't have to defend the premise because it was built into the term.

//

Think about that. Thousands of years of "economic theory" and NO ONE has asked, let alone answered, the fundamental question: Do we even need one?

Of what value are all these unbased theories, then?

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Great exposé on the corruption of science.

So now, everyone knows that even the very top echelons of our most important science—health—cannot only be corrupted, but can be the primary corruptor of the entire mess… because that’s exactly what it’s done. 

Even the deniers know it, which is why they're so desperately trying to Rah, Rah, Sis Boom Bah! this little asshole dweeb from the sidelines—like cheerleading is going to make a whit of difference, the idiots.

I guess y'all are going to have to abandon your cozy little fantasies about the trustworthiness of even your most pristine institutions and, for that matter, of anyone that's achieved an authoritative position in them. 

At this point, the only ones still insisting that we rely on our "experts" and "leaders" are power cultists who get stars in their eyes for anyone who stands up on a stage or in front of a camera or has a K after their number of followers. 

For the others of you still capable of rational thought, what are you going to do now?

What you should do and you need to do hasn't even occurred to you yet, which is why I bring it up. 

The codependent tendency towards delusion that induced you to idolize a smarmy, smug, squat little man and not realize what he was doing is the same tendency that gives you the impression that there was ever a time when science actually served the truth and, in turn, the benefit and welfare of us "commoners".

The myth of "do no harm" and the bullshit promise of greater health and longevity are precisely the carrots they used to get us to pull the carts full of mostly children and drag them off to the experimentation camps.

"Oh but the wonders of science! We do live longer and we are healthier!"

1. No, we do not and we are not—we did and we were, for a while.  What's more, the numbers which tell us that we did and were don’t include medical science’s and medical practice’s side effects and failures. An entire malpractice insurance industry does not exist because malpractice is so rare, dumbo. At this point, as of now, iatrogenic interventions are the number one leading cause of death in the United States. But no one wants to talk about that mid-room elephant. You won’t see it on the official lists. You can't say that science cures while you obstinately ignore when science kills and dumbshitly deny that it does—often. Both my mother and my sister died that way. 

2. The lion's share of huge health improvements in the 20th century did not come from medical science but from the institution of properly sanitary systems to provide clean water and deal effectively with waste and sewage—but medical science was all too happy to hop on that pony and pretend it owns a horse.

3. At this point, right now, we are the most obese, chronically ill, unhealthy specimens of humanity that might ever have walked the planet.

Medical science was not recently corrupted. Science of every type has always been the domain of the “rich”. 

Science that could potentially upset their interests is never conducted. 

Science that is conducted but that produces findings that could potentially upset their interests is always either quashed or corrupted or flat out falsified. 

And a shitload of science contrived to further their interests was nothing but patent nonsense, as becomes clear in every generation looking back on the science of the generations that by then had passed away.

Science has always served the ruling class “elites”, not you and me. And what have things come to when the elites of the world are the scum of humankind? 

The benefits we've enjoyed from science have been either incidental or strategic. 

And now, it’s clear what the whole shebang was contrived for. At this point, science not only sets no one free—it’s designed to do the exact opposite.

The “rich” do not love you. Their sciences do not love you. The authoritarianism it all serves does not love you. 

And they never did. 

You are the specimens, not the beneficiaries. You are the “human resources”, not the investors. You are the targets, not the clients.

You're going to have to deal with these facts sooner or later, and at the rate that the revelations keep coming—it’s only accelerating—judgment day be way sooner than you think. 

You might as well get started on adjusting yourself to reality, to the facts, now rather than procrastinate. 

It certainly won't be any easier on you later.
